name: ACPL-W343-560E
title: 4.0 A rail-to-rail output optocoupler for IGBT gates, stretched SO-6
summary: ACPL-P343 and ACPL-W343 are single-channel gate drive optocouplers: an AlGaAs LED lights a receiver IC whose PMOS/NMOS output stage swings rail to rail and sources or sinks up to 4.0 A peak (3.0 A minimum) into an IGBT or MOSFET gate. The output side runs from 15 V to 30 V with under-voltage lockout, the LED input has threshold hysteresis, propagation delay is 200 ns maximum and common-mode transient immunity is at least 35 kV/µs. ACPL-W343 has 8 mm clearance and a 5000 Vrms isolation rating; ACPL-P343 has 7 mm and 3750 Vrms.

notes: An order code joins a base number (ACPL-P343 or ACPL-W343) to an option suffix. All options are RoHS compliant. The two bases differ in package body and lead span: ACPL-P343 has 7 mm clearance, ACPL-W343 8 mm.

pins.name: NC
pins.function: Not connected inside. For the CMR figures it is tied to the LED common (the input-side ground).

pins.name: VEE
pins.function: Negative supply and return of the output stage. In the recommended application circuit it sits 5 V below the IGBT emitter.

pins.name: VOUT
pins.function: Gate drive output, pulled to VCC by a PMOS and to VEE by an NMOS. High while the LED is lit and VCC is above the UVLO level.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Positive supply of the output stage, 15 V to 30 V above VEE. Needs a 1 µF capacitor from VCC to VEE.

circuits.title: Recommended application circuit with split resistors LED drive
circuits.description: The optocoupler drives the high-side IGBT Q1 of one inverter leg. A pulse source on the controller side feeds the LED through a split pair of resistors R, one in the anode lead and one in the cathode lead, in a 1.5 : 1 ratio; the balanced resistance on both LED leads gives high CMR. The output side floats on Q1's emitter, which is the output-side ground: a 15 V supply sits above the emitter for VCC and a 5 V supply below it for VEE, so the gate swings from +15 V to -5 V relative to the emitter. A 1 µF capacitor across VCC and VEE carries the switching current pulses, and Rg in series with VOUT limits the gate charge current and sets the collector voltage rise and fall times. Q2 is the low-side IGBT of the same leg; the leg's midpoint is the AC output.

parts.note: high side; pins G, C, E
low side; pins G, C, E

notes: Q1 and Q2 are one leg of a three-phase IGBT bridge; the other two legs have the same form, each with its own phase output.
VCC is 15 V for an IGBT and 12 V for a MOSFET.

circuits.title: Recommended high-CMR drive circuit
circuits.description: An input stage for best common-mode rejection. From a 5 V rail, R1 (205 Ω) feeds the anode and R2 (137 Ω) returns the cathode to ground, so the two current-setting resistors sit on both LED leads in a ratio of about 1.5. An NPN transistor from the anode node to ground shunts the LED: with the transistor on the LED is held off, with it off the LED conducts through R1 and R2. Pin 2 is open.
notes: The resistor values are for VDD = 5.0 V.

circuits.title: IOH test circuit
circuits.description: Measures the high-level peak output current. The LED carries 7 to 16 mA from a current source. VCC is 15 to 30 V across VCC and VEE with a 1 µF bypass, and a pulsed 4 V source from VCC to VOUT pulls the output 4 V below VCC while IOH is measured.

circuits.title: IOL test circuit
circuits.description: Measures the low-level peak output current. The LED pins are left open, so the output is low. VCC is 15 to 30 V with a 1 µF bypass, and a pulsed 2.5 V source from VEE to VOUT holds the output 2.5 V above VEE while IOL is measured.

circuits.title: VOH test circuit
circuits.description: Measures the high-level output voltage. The LED carries 7 to 16 mA, VCC is 15 to 30 V with a 1 µF bypass, and a 100 mA current sink loads VOUT to VEE; VOH is read at VOUT.

circuits.title: VOL test circuit
circuits.description: Measures the low-level output voltage. The LED pins are open, VCC is 15 to 30 V with a 1 µF bypass, and a 100 mA current source feeds VOUT from VCC; VOL is read at VOUT.

circuits.title: IFLH test circuit
circuits.description: Finds the input threshold current. A ramping current source drives the LED; VCC is 15 to 30 V with a 1 µF bypass, and VOUT is loaded by 10 Ω in series with 25 nF to VEE. IFLH is the LED current at which VO rises past 5 V.

circuits.title: UVLO test circuit
circuits.description: Finds the under-voltage lockout thresholds. The LED carries 7 to 16 mA while VCC is ramped up and back down across a 1 µF bypass; the thresholds are the supply levels at which VO crosses 5 V.

circuits.title: tPLH, tPHL, tr and tf test circuit
circuits.description: Measures propagation delays and output edges. The LED is pulsed at 7 to 16 mA, 20 kHz, 50% duty cycle; VCC is 15 to 30 V with a 1 µF bypass, and VOUT drives 10 Ω in series with 25 nF to VEE, standing in for a gate. Delays are taken from the LED current edges to the 50% point of VOUT; rise and fall times run between the 20% and 80% points.

parts.value: IF = 7 to 16 mA, 20 kHz, 50% duty cycle

circuits.title: CMR test circuit with split resistors network
circuits.description: Measures common-mode transient immunity. On the input side a 5 V source feeds the anode through 205 Ω and a switch; the cathode returns to input ground through 137 Ω, and pin 2 is tied to that ground. Switch at A gives IF = 10 mA (output high, CMH); switch at B shorts the anode to ground, IF = 0 (output low, CML). The output side runs on VCC = 30 V with a 1 µF bypass, its ground at VEE. A 1500 V pulse generator between the two grounds applies the common-mode edge while VO is watched.

parts.value: SPDT, A = LED on, B = LED off

equations.expr: PDDMAX = (tPHL - tPLH)MAX = tPHL MAX - tPLH MIN
equations.note: Both delays are taken under identical temperature and conditions. Delaying one leg's LED turn-on by PDDMAX (100 ns) after the other leg's LED turn-off gives zero minimum dead time.

equations.expr: Dead timeMAX = (tPHL MAX - tPHL MIN) + (tPLH MAX - tPLH MIN) = PDDMAX - PDDMIN

operation.text: An AlGaAs LED on the input side shines across the isolation gap onto a photodetector IC. The detector feeds a Schmitt trigger and a power output stage built in BCDMOS: a PMOS from VCC to VOUT and an NMOS from VOUT to VEE. The part drives IGBTs rated up to 1200 V / 200 A directly; larger IGBTs take a discrete booster stage between the part and the gate.

Because the high side is a PMOS, VOUT pulls fully to VCC (VOH typically VCC - 0.2 V at 100 mA, VCC with no load), so the gate reaches the intended voltage without the three VBE drops of a Darlington output and without a pull-down resistor to fix the high level. This holds when the supply is not well regulated, which suits bootstrap supplies.

The receiver has a built-in Schmitt trigger, so the output edges are clean without extra wave shaping. The LED current threshold has hysteresis (IFLH, typically 1.5 mA), giving immunity to differential noise and keeping the output from chattering when the LED current is marginal.

While VCC - VEE is below the UVLO level the output is held low, including during power-up, so the IGBT never sees a weak gate drive. The output follows the LED once VCC rises past VUVLO+ (12.1 to 13.5 V) and is clamped low again when VCC falls below VUVLO- (11.1 to 12.4 V); hysteresis is about 1.0 V. IGBTs typically need 15 V of gate drive for their rated VCE(ON); below about 13 V VCE(ON) rises steeply, and below about 10 V the IGBT can run linear and overheat.

A 1 µF capacitor from VCC to VEE is required; it supplies the peak gate current during each transition. Average supply current is low (3.0 mA maximum), so a small supply serves. VCC of 15 V is recommended for an IGBT and 12 V for a MOSFET, adjusted to the switch's gate threshold.

Rg limits the gate charging current and so sets how fast the IGBT collector voltage slews. Pick its minimum from the peak output current, then check the part's dissipation (PO below 700 mW at 85 °C) and raise Rg if needed.

Common-mode edges couple through the stray capacitances CLA (anode to output side) and CLC (cathode to output side). If the currents through them, ILP and ILN, do not cancel, the LED current shifts momentarily: a drop while the LED is on can fail CMH, and a rise while it is off can lift the output above 1 V and fail CML. Splitting the current-setting resistance between anode and cathode (about 1.5 : 1, 205 Ω and 137 Ω at 5 V) balances the two paths, and a transistor that shunts the LED in the off state improves CML further. CMH depends on the LED current; with IF near the threshold IFLH it also depends on how closely ILP and ILN balance.

Dead time is the interval in which both transistors of a leg are off. The PDD limits (-100 ns to 100 ns over -40 °C to 105 °C) let a designer set the LED skew between the two drivers of a leg: skew equal to PDDMAX (100 ns) guarantees no overlap, and the resulting dead time from the optocouplers is at most 200 ns. The PDD figures assume both parts at the same temperature and conditions, as when they sit close together and drive identical IGBTs.
Keep IGBT collector and emitter traces away from the input side of the part; transients coupled into the input degrade performance.

The four thermal resistances R11, R12, R21 and R22 couple LED and detector heating to each junction. They were measured with the part soldered to a 7.62 cm × 7.62 cm JEDEC board, the ambient sensed about 1.25 cm above the part at about 23 °C in still air.
Driving IGBT and MOSFET gates: motor drives (AC and brushless DC), inverters for industry and for renewable energy, switching power supplies.
Reflow per JEDEC J-STD-020 (latest revision) with non-halide flux.
